item.aggregated_output: /home/ryan/work/code/personal/taryx ?? docs/project/evidence/m1c/m1c-events-r1.jsonl ?? docs/project/evidence/m1c/m1c-session-bootstrap.md 230dc0f1078243e3448ecc145c842228b22cca8c # Taryx documentation guide Created: 2026-10-25 Scope: Project planning, task tracking, decisions, verification evidence, and work records in Taryx. ## Purpose and source of truth Use Markdown to preserve what we intend to build, what is agreed, what comes next, what is blocked, and what has actually been verified. This workflow adapts Cateniq's conventions to Taryx's single-repository boundary. Taryx owns its records independently; Cateniq and Voltix are references, not shared trackers. Canonical documents live in `docs/project/`, relative to the Taryx root. The repository README is the entry point. Do not maintain another project README or duplicate backlog elsewhere. If preserved locally, `docs/initial-discussion/` files are background discussions and proposals. The original planning chats currently live outside this repository; the README and canonical planning records capture the reconciled direction without depending on those local files. Preserve them as source material. Their titles, including “Final,” do not establish current acceptance. During planning, reconcile them with the user's agreements and later review findings, then link from the canonical specifications. Do not silently promote every suggestion into an accepted requirement. ## File layout and ownership ```text README.md Introduction, verified setup, documentation links AGENTS.md Scoped agent workflow instructions .devin/skills/project-management/ Portable project-management skill docs/initial-discussion/ Preserved background proposals and conversations docs/agent-notes/ Tooling notes and agent workarounds (non-canonical) docs/project/ documentation-guide.md Process, templates, and record ownership roadmap.md Milestones, scope, dependencies, exit criteria backlog.md Canonical task records and status architecture.md Current design and acceptance/implementation status blockers.md Obstacles and unresolved decision gates features/*.md Behaviour and acceptance specifications, when needed decisions/001-short-title.md Significant decisions and their reasoning evidence// Sanitised verification findings, when needed journal/YYYY-MM.md Historical work outcomes and verification ``` The root `README.md` preserves motivation, portfolio context and source links. Canonical architecture, feature contracts and task records own evolving implementation details; link to them rather than maintaining a second plan in the concept document. Create feature specifications and evidence documents only when they have useful content. This setup does not require empty future directories or a preselected implementation backlog. | Record | Owns | Update when | | --- | --- | --- | | `README.md` | Introduction, setup, navigation | Setup or documentation locations change; do not duplicate task status here | | `documentation-guide.md` | Workflow and templates | The process or tracking ownership changes | | `roadmap.md` | Milestone scope, dependencies, exit criteria, progress | Scope or sequence changes, work begins, or exit criteria pass | | `backlog.md` | Task IDs, priorities, status, acceptance and completion evidence | Work is refined, started, blocked, completed, reopened, or dropped | | `architecture.md` | Boundaries, components, interfaces, persistence and deployment design | Design is accepted or implementation changes it | | `blockers.md` | Questions, impact, evidence, unblock actions and resolutions | An obstacle is identified, investigated, or resolved | | `features/*.md` | Behaviour, inputs, outputs, rules, failure cases and acceptance | Before implementation and when agreed behaviour changes | | `decisions/*.md` | Context, choice, alternatives, consequences and acceptance source | A significant choice is proposed, accepted, rejected, or superseded | | `evidence//` | Reproducible checks, observations and limitations | Verification needs detail beyond a task's short completion evidence | | `journal/YYYY-MM.md` | Dated outcomes, checks, model/agent attribution | A meaningful work unit concludes or reaches a useful partial outcome | Prefer links over repeated explanations. Task status belongs in tasks, milestone status in the roadmap, reasoning in decisions, and historical outcomes in the journal. ## Roadmap conventions Taryx milestones live in the roadmap and are established through project planning. Do not copy Cateniq's or Voltix's milestones or automatically adopt the sequence in an initial discussion document. For each agreed milestone record: - Outcome and included scope. - Exclusions and dependencies. - Observable exit criteria and linked tasks/evidence. - Status: `Planned`, `In progress`, or `Complete`. Detail the upcoming milestone and immediate dependencies; keep later work broad. Mark completion only when exit criteria are satisfied. Distinguish local verification, hosted CI, native service verification, and release readiness where relevant. If a gate is deferred, explicitly record the accepted scope change and follow-up; do not silently claim it passed. ## Task records Initially keep task bodies in `backlog.md`. Assign sequential IDs starting at `TAR-001`; never reuse an ID. IDs identify tasks, not priority. Maintain a compact index in ascending ID order, using a leading status icon and a link to each task. Append new task links at the end. Task sections own the status word; index icons mirror it. Put delivery order and next-work context in `Delivery notes`, not in index ordering. Use explicit anchors for stable links: ```markdown ## TAR-XXX — Short outcome-oriented title - Repository: taryx - Area: documentation | workspace | metering | pricing | billing | migration | integration | portal | verification | deployment - Milestone: agreed milestone, or Not assigned - Priority: High | Normal | Low - Status: Backlog 📋 | Ready 🟢 | In progress 🚧 | Blocked ⛔ | Done ✅ | Dropped 🗑️ - Depends on: task IDs, or None - References: specification and decision links ### Outcome Describe the concrete deliverable or behaviour. ### Done when - Observable acceptance criterion. - Relevant verification requirement. ### Completion evidence Actual checks and results, including failures or checks not run. Link commits/PRs when known. Otherwise identify changed files and uncommitted state. ### Notes Material context, blocker link, next action, or reason for reopening/dropping. ``` | State | Icon | Meaning | | --- | --- | --- | | Backlog | 📋 | Identified work needing refinement or prioritisation | | Ready | 🟢 | Scope and acceptance are clear; dependencies satisfied | | In progress | 🚧 | Actively underway; keep the active set small | | Blocked | ⛔ | A specific obstacle prevents progress; link its blocker | | Done | ✅ | Acceptance and required verification satisfied, with evidence | | Dropped | 🗑️ | Removed from scope deliberately, with a recorded reason | Write the icon after the status word in task sections, for example `Status: Done ✅`. Update the index icon whenever status changes. Several status icons are non-BMP (4-byte UTF-8) characters that the file-edit tools corrupt on write; apply icon changes with scripted writes and verify the bytes per [the emoji-corruption note](../agent-notes/emoji-corruption.md). Prefer tasks reviewable in a focused session. Split by meaningful outcome, not file count. Retain completed records. Required verification pending means the task is not Done. Reopen with a reason or create a follow-up for new scope. Minor edits need not manufacture a task. If the backlog becomes unwieldy, move bodies to `tasks/TAR-XXX-short-title.md` and retain the backlog as an index. Preserve IDs and links; do not maintain duplicate bodies. ## Blockers and open questions Use sequential stable IDs such as `BLK-001`. Record: - Identification date and the concrete question or obstacle. - Status: `Open` or `Resolved`. - Affected tasks/milestones and practical impact. - Whether it blocks current work or can be investigated alongside it. - Evidence, attempted approaches, and relevant links. - Next action and who or what can resolve it. - Resolution and date when resolved. Do not mark the whole project blocked because one task is blocked. Future planning decisions are not failed implementation attempts. Keep evidence and resolution here; tasks link to them. Record a lasting design choice in a decision record when warranted. ## Decision records Use numbered files such as `001-markdown-project-tracking.md` for material architecture, correctness, scope, or maintenance choices. Routine implementation details do not require a decision record. Each record contains title, date, status (`Proposed`, `Accepted`, `Rejected`, `Superseded`), context, decision, alternatives, consequences, follow-up, and relevant links. Accepted records must identify their acceptance source: explicit user agreement or a selection within delegated authority. Recommendations alone are not acceptance. When replacing a decision, preserve its original reasoning, mark it Superseded, and link to its replacement. Update the current specification or architecture separately. Accepted design is not proof of implementation or verification. ## Verification evidence Record the command or procedure, environment, inputs/workload, observed result, and limitations. Link detailed findings from the affected task when useful. Distinguish passing, failing, skipped, and unavailable checks. Keep synthetic/simulated results distinct from hardware observations, and local results distinct from hosted CI or deployment results. Do not claim guarantees broader than the evidence. Keep secrets and unsanitised sensitive responses out of all records. Avoid committing bulky generated outputs when a concise reproducible procedure and findings suffice. ## Session workflow ### Before work 1. Read this guide, roadmap, and backlog to identify the current outcome and next task. 2. Read relevant specifications, architecture sections, decisions, and blockers. 3. Inspect actual files and repository state; documentation may lag. 4. Confirm acceptance criteria/dependencies and mark the task In progress when beginning it. ### During work 1. Stay within the authorised scope; record useful newly discovered work separately. 2. Update specifications when agreed behaviour changes. 3. Record material decisions, blockers, and actual verification results. 4. Preserve unrelated changes. When several agents contribute, coordinate task/file ownership and reconcile their evidence before marking the overall task Done. ### Before ending meaningful work 1. Update affected tasks with status, evidence, remaining work, and the next action. 2. Update affected architecture/specifications and blockers. 3. Change milestone status only when its exit criteria warrant it. 4. Add one concise journal entry for the work unit, or amend its existing entry. 5. Check links, status/index consistency, and contradictions across changed records. Apply this after implementation, substantive investigation, accepted planning decisions, or documentation deliverables without a separate reminder. Pure explanations and unchanged status checks need no edits. Documentation closeout does not trigger another journal entry about itself. When an authorised commit occurs, include related records in the same commit as the change they describe. Record changed files or a branch/PR in the journal rather than trying to include its own commit SHA. Reserve standalone `Records:` commits for record-only corrections. This workflow does not itself authorise commits, pushes, external tracker changes, publication, or scheduled automation. ### At milestone boundaries Review exit criteria, evidence, outstanding tasks, and blockers. Mark completion only when supported, then refine the next milestone. Preserve explicit verification gaps rather than describing local completion as release readiness. ## Journal format and time Use monthly files named for the UTC entry date. Read the system clock, for example `date -u`, rather than estimating or converting local time manually. Journal headings use `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC`. Ordinary planning dates may use the user's local date (Australia/Sydney); label times explicitly when ambiguity matters. ```markdown ## YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC — Short work outcome - LLM model: Reliable session-reported model; note unknown variant details. - Coding agent: Agent/application; version only if known. - Tasks: TAR-XXX, or None for work without a task. - Completed: Concrete outcome or meaningful partial result. - Verification: Checks performed and actual outcomes, including limitations. - Remaining: Next action or links to unfinished tasks/blockers. - Changes: Commit/PR references, or changed files if uncommitted. ``` Every entry includes separate LLM model and coding agent fields. Do not infer model identity from the agent name, available-model lists, or defaults. If only the family is known, record it and say the exact variant is unavailable. Use `Unknown (not recorded)` where no reliable evidence exists. List multiple contributors and their roles when relevant. Keep entries short; do not copy transcripts or entire acceptance checklists. Correct factual errors without erasing the history of what was known at the time. Do not duplicate this journal in another location. ## Maintenance The project-root `AGENTS.md` activates this workflow through the `project-management` skill, with a repository-carried copy at `.devin/skills/project-management/SKILL.md`. If it is unavailable, read this guide and restore the repository copy; do not introduce machine-local dependencies. It is a session routine, not a background watcher. Reconcile interrupted work at the next session. Update only affected records. Preserve discussion sources and completed history. If an external tracker is adopted later, migrate task ownership and stop maintaining a second Markdown task tracker; retain specifications, architecture, decisions, and operational documentation in the repository and update this guide. --- name: project-management description: Maintain Taryx's Markdown roadmap, tasks, decisions, blockers, and work journal per docs/project/documentation-guide.md. Use for meaningful Taryx work and after implementation, investigation, planning decisions, or documentation updates. allowed-tools: - read - grep - glob - edit - exec --- # Project management and documentation Keep Taryx's durable project records aligned with actual work. This is an in-session workflow, not a background watcher or scheduled task. ## Establish the source of truth - Read the root `AGENTS.md` instructions and `docs/project/documentation-guide.md`. The guide owns record locations, templates, task/blocker formats, statuses, timezone, and update rules — follow it exactly. - Read only the roadmap, active tasks, and specifications/decisions relevant to the work. Reconcile records with code, verification output, and the current conversation. - Treat `docs/initial-discussion/` as preserved background proposals. Their titles and embedded suggestions do not establish acceptance; reconcile them with user agreements and link them from canonical records. - Inspect actual files and repository state before updating records; documentation may lag reality. ## Update after meaningful work Before the final response following implementation, a substantive investigation, an accepted planning decision, or a documentation deliverable: 1. Update the affected task in `docs/project/backlog.md` with actual status, completion evidence, remaining work, and the next concrete action. Reuse its `TAR-XXX` ID. Add a task for newly identified work only when useful under the guide's conventions; do not invent historical IDs or manufacture a ticket for every minor edit. 2. Update feature specifications for changed behaviour and `docs/project/architecture.md` for changed technical design. Keep proposed, accepted, implemented, and verified states distinct; recommendations are not acceptance. 3. Record material obstacles and unresolved questions in `docs/project/blockers.md` with affected tasks, impact, evidence, and an unblock action. Resolve existing records when evidence supports it. 4. Update milestone status in `docs/project/roadmap.md` only when its exit criteria warrant it. Preserve agreed scope and sequencing. 5. Add one concise journal entry for the completed work unit or meaningful partial outcome in `docs/project/journal/YYYY-MM.md`, following the guide's format. Include verification performed, limitations, and task/commit/PR links when available. Mark uncommitted work honestly. Read the system clock (`date -u`) for the UTC timestamp and record LLM model and coding agent as separate fields; write `Unknown (not recorded)` rather than guessing. 6. Check consistency and references among affected files. Briefly mention material documentation updates in the final response. Update only affected records. If an answer is purely explanatory, a status check reveals no change, or the same outcome has already been recorded, make no documentation edit. If repeating this workflow for the same work unit, amend the existing entry rather than append a duplicate. Documentation updates do not themselves trigger another round of journaling. ## Evidence and scope - A task is Done only when acceptance criteria and required verification are satisfied. Report failed, skipped, or unavailable checks; do not claim that a commit, deployment, or test occurred without evidence. - Keep status in the backlog, milestone progress in the roadmap, reasoning in decisions, and historical outcomes in the journal. Prefer links to duplicate explanations. - Preserve completed records and decision history. Supersede outdated decisions rather than silently rewriting their original reasoning. - Do not overwrite unrelated work, bootstrap every missing document during routine closeout, or rewrite the backlog based on guesses. If a required record cannot be updated, state the specific limitation and next action. - Status icons and other non-BMP characters are corrupted by the `edit`/`write` tools; apply those changes with scripted writes and verify the bytes — see `docs/agent-notes/emoji-corruption.md`. - This workflow does not authorise commits, pushes, messages, external tracker mutations, or scheduled automations. Preserve the user's existing authorisation scope.

# Metering and rating

Date: 2026-10-25
Status: Supported subset, time conventions and numeric profile frozen by TAR-004 on 2026-10-25; quality-method and 400-record semantics corrected the same day after the [independent M1 review](../evidence/m1/m1-exit-review.md) against MDFF v2.7. [BLK-001](../blockers.md#blk-001) resolved. Reference cases live in [rating-reference-cases.md](rating-reference-cases.md).
Tasks: [TAR-004](../backlog.md#tar-004), [TAR-005](../backlog.md#tar-005), [TAR-006](../backlog.md#tar-006).

## User outcome

An operator imports synthetic interval data, sees accepted/rejected records and provenance, and can explain the quantities and rates behind each bill line. Supported tariffs begin with daily supply, time-of-use import and solar export credits. Demand charges, wholesale pass-through and VPP incentives are excluded initially.

## Inputs and history

Record supply point, meter/channel, direction, interval boundaries, unit, quality, source batch/hash and source revision information. Preserve raw source evidence and revisions; do not overwrite previous readings. A stable interval identity and explicit source precedence determine the current selection, not arrival order. Duplicate batches and repeated revisions are no-ops with inspectable results. Equal-precedence conflicting values are quarantined for review, not silently selected.

Validate file size, supported records, interval lengths, units, ordering and supply-point references. Stage a batch before publishing its accepted revision set; parsing failure must not leave a partially current billing dataset. If chunked ingestion is chosen, freeze its atomic visibility contract before implementation. Invalid or incomplete coverage blocks issuance by default; no silent zero filling or invented estimates.

## Frozen calculation inputs

The billing period uses half-open boundaries and carries its time convention explicitly. NEM meter timestamps, tariff civil time and UTC storage must be distinguished. TAR-004 must resolve interval-end conventions, daylight-saving transitions, leap days and effective-date changes against authoritative format documentation. Do not assume every day has 288 civil-time intervals or every NEM12 record is five-minute data.

Record selected reading revisions, tariff version, agreement effective dates, client policy identity and calculation engine version in an immutable snapshot. Use Decimal for quantities and rates, with explicit units and rounding points. Tariff changes inside a period split calculations according to effective dates. Missing, overlapping or ambiguous agreements produce explicit errors.

## Evidence and acceptance

- Hand-worked reference cases independently verify flat/time-of-use charges, export credits, daily charges and chosen tax/rounding rules.
- A tariff boundary, leap day and applicable daylight-saving boundary have explicit expected quantities and amounts.
- Duplicate, out-of-order, conflicting and corrected readings preserve provenance and deterministic selection.
- Malformed input, unsupported interval/unit, incomplete coverage and unknown meters fail visibly.
- Re-running the same snapshot produces the same itemised result and digest.
- Seed fixtures carry deterministic generator parameters, intended defects and independent expected results; expected results must not be computed by the engine under test.

Australian regulatory/tax claims require linked authoritative sources in the frozen profile. Fictional retailer policies are labelled as such. Implementation is blocked on the relevant profile decisions, not on the entire project.

## Frozen profile (TAR-004, 2026-10-25)

### Authoritative references

- [MDFF Specification NEM12 & NEM13, v2.7 (AEMO, 2025)](https://aemo.com.au/-/media/files/electricity/nem/retail_and_metering/market_settlement_and_transfer_solutions/2025/mdff-specification-nem12-nem13-v27.pdf) — record layout, blocking order, quality method 'V', reason-code rules, IntervalDate sequencing.
- [Metrology Procedure Part B (AEMO, v8.12 consultation draft)](https://www.aemo.com.au/-/media/files/stakeholder_consultation/consultations/nem-consultations/2025/october-2025-remp/final-stage/metrology-procedure-part-b-v812-clean.pdf) — quality flag meanings and replacement rules (also present in earlier released versions).
- [AEMO EMMS Data Model v5.4](https://tech-specs.docs.public.aemo.com.au/Content/TSP_EMMSDM54_Oct2024/EMMS_DMv5.4_Nov24.pdf) — "INTERVAL_DATETIME … fixed to the UTC+10 time zone (NEM time)"; interval-ending timestamps.
- [Project EDGE Data Specification Part A (AEMO)](https://www.aemo.com.au/-/media/files/initiatives/der/2023/project-edge---data-specification-part-a.pdf) — "NEM time … defined as AEST which is 10 hrs ahead of UTC".
- GST rate: 10% under the A New Tax System (Goods and Services Tax) Act 1999; GST-inclusive component = amount ÷ 11 (sourced).
- Channel letters cross-checked against AEMO example-file conventions as documented by retailers (Ergon, Shell Energy NEM12 guides): `E*` registers are energy delivered from the grid to the site; `B1` is site generation exported to the grid.

### Supported format subset

| Aspect | Frozen support |
| --- | --- |
| File | CSV MDFF, `VersionHeader=NEM12`, exactly one 100 and one 900 record, blocking order 100→200→300(→400)→900; record 500 (B2B) ignored if present but not required |
| Records parsed | 100 header, 200 NMI data details, 300 interval data, 400 interval event, 900 end |
| IntervalLength | 30 or 5 minutes only |
| Unit of measure | `kWh` only |
| Channels | `E*` registers (grid-delivered import) and `B1` (site generation export); other suffix letters rejected |
| Encoding | UTF-8 text; undecodable bytes are rejected at the byte boundary |
| IntervalValue | Plain non-negative decimal, `^\d{1,9}(\.\d{1,6})?$`; signs, exponents and non-finite values rejected |
| QualityMethod | `QMM` form: one-letter flag `A`/`S`/`E`/`F` plus optional two-digit method code (e.g. `E52`, `S14`, `F12`); `A` carries no method; `V` is valid only on a 300 record. Method codes are retained as `method_code` metadata and not interpreted |
| ReasonCode | Required on `S`/`F` intervals (per MDFF 3.3.5); optional on `A`/`E`/`V`-derived intervals; numeric ≤ 3 digits; retained as evidence, not interpreted |
| 400 records | `400,StartInterval,EndInterval,QualityMethod,ReasonCode,ReasonDescription` applying to the immediately preceding 300 record. Ranges must tile the entire day in ascending order without gaps or overlaps; the ranged QualityMethod/ReasonCode applies to every interval in the range; `V` is not permitted in a 400 record; intervals inherit the parent 300's UpdateDateTime/MSATSLoadDateTime. Mandatory where the 300 QualityMethod is `V`; also valid to carry reason codes on other days |

Rejected with explicit errors: NEM13 files, zipped archives, multiple header blocks, non-kWh UOM, interval lengths other than 5/30, non-E/B suffixes, unknown NMI references, out-of-order 300 records, malformed/truncated records, invalid interval values, `S`/`F` flags without reason codes, and gapped/overlapping or missing 400 coverage.

### Time conventions

- All interval timestamps are **NEM time**: AEST, fixed UTC+10, no daylight saving (sourced). Stored internally as UTC instants; civil-time (e.g. Australia/Sydney) conversion happens only at presentation boundaries.
- Timestamps are **interval-ending**: interval *n* of IntervalDate *d* covers `(d 00:00 + (n-1)L, d 00:00 + nL]` NEM time. The value stamped 00:30 covers 00:00–00:30.
- Every NEM day therefore has exactly 48 (30-min) or 288 (5-min) intervals — including days that are 23/25 hours in civil time. DST transitions cannot produce partial NEM days; they only shift which UTC/civil instants the NEM day maps to.
- Billing periods are half-open `[start 00:00 NEM, end 00:00 NEM)` and carry the convention explicitly.
- The NEM *trading day* (04:00–04:00, settlement convention) is out of scope; retail billing aligns to NEM calendar days.

### Revision selection and conflicts

1. Quality precedence `A` > `F` > `S` > `E` selects the current value per interval (consistent with the metrology replacement rules: higher-ranked flags may replace lower-ranked ones). The method-code suffix does not participate in precedence.
2. Within equal quality, the record with the latest `MSATSLoadDateTime`, then `UpdateDateTime`, wins; batch/record identity breaks remaining ties deterministically.
3. Equal-precedence conflicting values are quarantined for operator review — never silently selected. All top-precedence rivals are retained on the quarantine record for investigation.
4. Publication is optimistic under concurrency: candidates are evaluated once without locks, then every affected interval is re-evaluated and written under its per-interval row lock in deterministic order. A racing publisher therefore cannot regress the current selection with stale candidates.
5. An unambiguous newer winner resolves an open quarantine (marked resolved with history retained); only open quarantines block billing coverage.
6. A new effective revision marks dependent calculations stale; issued bills are never rewritten.

### Numeric and tax profile

- Decimal arithmetic end-to-end. Interval quantities: full precision (no rounding on read). Money: `ROUND_HALF_UP` to 2 dp **per bill line**, then summed (fictional-retailer policy, frozen for testability).
- Rates are GST-exclusive. GST = 10% of GST-applicable lines, computed per line at 2 dp (sourced rate; applicability matrix below is fictional policy).
- GST applies to supply-charge and consumption lines. Export feed-in credits are treated as non-GST (fictional simplification; real FIT GST treatment varies by customer registration).
- Feed-in credit reduces the bill total; a net-negative bill is allowed and surfaces as a credit adjustment scenario.
- Tariff versions carry effective `[start, end)` dates in NEM time; a change inside a billing period splits calculation at the boundary. Missing/overlapping/ambiguous agreements are explicit errors.

### Exclusions (explicit)

NEM13/accumulated data, demand (kW/kVAr) registers, `Q`/`K`/`N` suffixes, NET-metered single-register files, AEMO substitution type 51–68 semantics, wholesale settlement, real customer data, and any claim of MSATS conformance.

## Measurement profile (TAR-004, closes BLK-003)

Reference environment (measured 2026-10-25): 14-core x86-64, 30 GiB RAM (~10 GiB free), NVMe SSD with 167 GiB free, Docker 29.7.2 / Compose v5.5.0, Linux 7.0. Idle stack baseline: ~1.2 GiB total across db/broker/api/worker/web; `/healthz` ≈ 18 ms; GraphQL ping ≈ 5.5 ms; taryx app image 391 MB.

| Rung | Workload | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1 (required) | 100 accounts × 30 NEM days × 48 intervals (30-min E1) + B1 on 25% of accounts ≈ 180k intervals | Frozen acceptance workload |
| R2 (optional) | 1 000 accounts × 30 NEM days × 288 intervals (5-min) ≈ 8.6 M intervals | Capacity experiment, clearly labelled |

Frozen budgets (initial, R1, on the reference environment):

- Ingest R1 end-to-end ≤ 90 s wall clock.
- Billing run ≤ 2 s per account p95; R1 batch ≤ 5 min total.
- API read p95 ≤ 500 ms during ingestion; no false completed operations under faults.
- Worker SIGKILL recovery ≤ 60 s with exactly one financial effect per operation.
- Stack memory ≤ 8 GiB during R1; no unbounded queue growth.

# Devin-driven Codex review loop (simplified process)

Status: pilot convention, agreed 2026-11-08; revised same day after a
Codex self-audit (`codex-review-loop-audit.md` — its findings are
adopted selectively here; recommendations there are not all binding).
The project-agnostic mechanism now lives in the global
`codex-review-loop` skill (linked from `campaign`); this document is
the Taryx instance — session ids, evidence paths, and observed quirks.
Predecessors: `multi-agent-handoff-problem.md` (problem framing),
`multi-agent-orchestrator-research.md` (what takt/ccbridge do).

## Purpose

Run a milestone's implement/review cycle with one human "go" message
instead of the user relaying "Devin has done M{N}, can you review" /
"Codex reviewed, can you resolve" between the two desktop apps.

Devin (this Devin Desktop session) is the loop driver. Codex runs as a
synchronous subprocess invoked through its CLI against the **existing**
review thread, so review context accumulates across milestones.

## Actors and mechanism

- **Implementer / driver**: Devin, inside this Devin Desktop session.
  Implements, commits, remediates, and invokes the reviewer.
- **Reviewer**: a dedicated Codex *exec session* per milestone, invoked
  via `codex exec resume <session-id>` from
  `/usr/lib/chatgpt/resources/codex`. A fresh session is created for
  each milestone and resumed across that milestone's remediation
  rounds — a perpetual thread accumulates bias toward its own earlier
  verdicts and compacts away qualifications, so context beyond one
  milestone lives in the repo (review docs, probes), not the session.
  (The desktop-app thread `Taryx project review`,
  `01a16e5a-546f-7850-8796-1484463b943f`, was evaluated and rejected —
  its managed profile is read-only; see "Reviewer permissions".)
- **Mutual exclusion**: between the two agents, structural — while
  `codex exec` runs, Devin is blocked waiting on the subprocess. This
  is *not* an OS lock: other processes (a human editor, a second
  `codex` attach) can still touch the tree. The git-state gate in step
  2 is what detects outside interference.
- **Turn boundary**: the `codex exec` process exit.

### Hard thread rule

`codex exec resume` fails with `thread ... already has an active writer`
if the session is held open elsewhere — e.g. the thread open in the
Codex desktop app, or another `codex` process attached to it. During a
loop run the review session must not be open anywhere else; on a lock
conflict Devin stops and asks rather than retrying.

## The loop

For each milestone M{N}, after implementation and its commit:

1. **Review invocation** — Devin runs:

   ```bash
   /usr/lib/chatgpt/resources/codex exec -C "$REPO" --approve-for-me \
     resume <session-id> \
     --output-schema docs/project/evidence/verdict.schema.json \
     --json \
     -o docs/project/evidence/m{N}-verdict-r{R}.json \
     "M{N} implementation is committed at <sha>. Review per our
      conventions: write findings to
      docs/project/evidence/m{N}-independent-review.md plus runnable
      pytest probes, and update affected project records. Do not
      commit."
   ```

   Exec-level options (`-C`, `--approve-for-me`, `-c`) go **before**
   `resume` — they are not resume's own options. `--json` tees the
   event stream to stdout (capture it into
   `m{N}-events-r{R}.jsonl`); `--output-schema` constrains the final
   message, which `-o` saves — the verdict is a JSON artifact, not a
   prose marker. The human-readable review lives in the repo files
   Codex writes, not in `-o`.

   The review session is provisioned **once per milestone**, before
   its first round:

   ```bash
   /usr/lib/chatgpt/resources/codex exec -C "$REPO" --approve-for-me \
     -c 'sandbox_workspace_write.network_access=true' \
     "You are the independent reviewer for Taryx milestone M{N}.
      Review conventions live in docs/project/documentation-guide.md
      and docs/agent-notes/. Reply READY." \
     -o docs/project/evidence/m{N}-session-bootstrap.md
   ```

   Record the new session id (from the `--json` event stream or
   `session_index.jsonl`) in `handoff/state` or the journal — never
   use `--last` in automation.

   `--approve-for-me` selects workspace-write plus automatic review of
   approval requests. Verified 2026-11-08: sandboxed file writes work
   on both the create call and later `exec resume` rounds, and the
   audit run itself wrote docs/backlog/journal inside this repo.
   Whether automatic *escalation* (approval requests above the
   sandbox) survives resume is unverified — `approval_policy` drops
   to `never` on resume, which means "cannot ask", not "approve all".
   `network_access=true` enables broad command networking (not just
   localhost) and is needed for the dockerised Postgres on
   localhost:55432 — DB reachability on resume still needs a live
   round.

   Long reviews run as a backgrounded exec; Devin polls until exit.
   Record `git rev-parse HEAD` **and** `git status --porcelain`
   before the call.

2. **Gate checks on exit** — Devin verifies:

   - HEAD unchanged *and* the working tree matches its pre-call state
     except for allowed paths (`docs/`, probe files, `handoff/`).
     An unchanged HEAD does **not** prove the source is unchanged —
     staged, unstaged, and untracked writes must all be checked, and
     unexpected-path writes make the round fail, not approved.
   - The verdict JSON parses against the schema **and** its semantics:
     `reviewed_sha` equals the candidate SHA, verdict ∈
     `APPROVED | CHANGES_REQUESTED | BLOCKED`, required checks are
     present. `APPROVED` with missing checks or a SHA mismatch is
     rejected — schema compliance is not review correctness.
   - A crash, timeout, missing verdict, or unexpected write counts as
     an incomplete round, not an approval.

3. **Commit the docs first** — Codex's working-tree output (review doc,
   probes, record updates) is reviewed by Devin and committed as the
   first step of remediation, per the existing convention.

4. **Remediation** — if `CHANGES_REQUESTED`: Devin resolves findings,
   folds probes into the test suite, commits, then re-invokes step 1
   for the next round. The resumed thread carries prior-round context.

5. **Termination** — proceed to the next milestone only on
   `verdict: APPROVED` in the schema output **and** the preserved
   probes plus required project checks green. `BLOCKED` also ends the
   loop — straight to escalation.

6. **Escalation** — stop to the user after **3 rounds** without
   approval, on `verdict: BLOCKED`, or on any ambiguous state (lock
   conflict, unparsable verdict, unexpected writes, Codex blocked
   needing input). Do not loop indefinitely; an authorized extra round
   is recorded in loop state, not just conversation.

### Interruption and stop state

Quota and other process deaths (usage limits, timeouts, crashes) are
**incomplete rounds** — never approvals, never findings. Codex quota
(5-hour and weekly windows on the ChatGPT plan) is a shared
environmental constraint: a multi-milestone campaign can exhaust a
window mid-round, as happened at foundation R4 on 2026-11-08.

On any interrupted turn:

1. Keep the partial `m{N}-events-r{R}.jsonl` — it records how far the
   turn got, and the `turn.failed` payload carries the error and any
   suggested retry time.
2. Record the stop state in the journal: milestone, session id, round,
   candidate SHA, reason, retry time. This is what makes a later
   session resumable rather than archaeological.
3. Inspect — never blindly keep or discard — working-tree writes the
   died turn made; it may have been mid-review. Commit retained
   partial artifacts labelled as interrupted output.
4. Resume with `codex exec resume <same session id>` after the quota
   window resets — the session's context survives the failed turn.

## Standing rules (unchanged)

- Devin makes every commit; Codex makes none.
- `git push` is always manual — never prompted, never run by the loop.
- Review docs, preserved probes, and record updates follow
  `docs/project/documentation-guide.md`.

## Reviewer permissions

Observed 2026-11-08 (M3 loop, rounds 1–4): the `Taryx project review`
desktop thread runs a **managed restricted** profile — filesystem
read-only, `network: restricted`, `approval_policy: never`, and `cwd`
pinned to an unrelated project directory. It could source-review and
report findings via `-o`, but could not write docs/probes or run the
database tests.

**Why interactive chat feels fully-permitted**: the app thread answers
approval requests through `approvals_reviewer: auto_review` — an
automated reviewer grants scoped elevation per action. That is the
same thing `--approve-for-me` selects on the CLI; it is *not* the
`--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` mode.

**Why `exec resume` on that thread is read-only**: resume inherits the
*session's* profile. "Managed" does not prove every override is
ignored — admin requirements constrain overrides, but exact precedence
for that thread is unverified. The reliable fix is to resume a session
that was *created* with a writable profile.

Verified 2026-11-08 on this machine:

- `codex exec --approve-for-me` → `approval: on-request` (routed to
  auto-review), `sandbox: workspace-write [workdir, /tmp, $TMPDIR]` —
  wrote files and ran commands. The early probes wrote `/tmp` only.
- `codex exec resume <that-session>` → keeps `workspace-write`,
  `approval: never` — wrote files with no flags needed.
- The self-audit run (`codex exec -C taryx --approve-for-me
  -c 'sandbox_workspace_write.network_access=true'`) wrote
  `codex-review-loop-audit.md`, backlog, and journal entries directly
  into this repo — first live *repo* write evidence, not just `/tmp`.
- Still unverified: approval escalation above the sandbox on resume,
  and Postgres connectivity through the resumed session.

Options, in preference order:

1. **Dedicated exec session per milestone (adopted)** — fresh session
   per milestone, resumed across that milestone's rounds.
   Write/exec verified including repo paths. Not an app thread, so the
   writer-lock rule does not apply.
2. **New chat in the Codex "Taryx" project** on a trusted, writable
   project profile — equivalent permissions via the app profile, plus
   the transcript stays in the desktop UI. Writer-lock rule applies.
3. **`--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`** — disables Codex
   sandboxing and confirmations *where permitted*; it does not
   override OS, container, or admin-enforced restrictions. Emergency
   only — not required for the ordinary loop.
4. **Fallback (verified)** — restricted thread + `-o` verdict `.md`
   committed as the review artifact; Devin authors record updates.

## Known limitations

- **Thread lock**: app-open thread breaks `exec resume` (above).
- **Context growth**: resumed threads compact over many milestones; if
  the reviewer loses conventions, pin the review prompt text above or
  fall back to stateless rounds with the review doc as the contract.
- **No independent check on Devin**: the loop verifies Codex's output
  mechanically (HEAD, verdict file, probes) but Devin's own gates are
  self-enforced. Human review of commits before push remains the
  backstop.
- **`codex queue --thread` exists** for injecting messages while the
  app holds the thread, but delivery is async — not used by this loop.

## Human touchpoints per milestone

1. "Go on M{N}" — one message starts the whole cycle.
2. Escalations, if any (round cap, lock, blocked reviewer).
3. Review the commits and push manually when satisfied.
"""Deterministic current-interval selection per the frozen profile.

Precedence: quality A > F > S > E, then MSATSLoadDateTime, then
UpdateDateTime. Records tying on all three but differing in value are a
conflict (quarantine); identical values resolve deterministically by
batch/row recency so repeated revisions are no-ops.
"""

from datetime import UTC, datetime

from taryx.core.metering.models import IntervalRecord

QUALITY_RANK = {"A": 4, "F": 3, "S": 2, "E": 1}
_MIN_DT = datetime.min.replace(tzinfo=UTC)


def precedence(record: IntervalRecord) -> tuple:
    return (
        QUALITY_RANK.get(record.quality, 0),
        record.msats_load_dt or _MIN_DT,
        record.update_dt or _MIN_DT,
    )


def _order(record: IntervalRecord) -> tuple:
    return precedence(record) + (record.batch_id, record.row_number)


def select_current(records: list[IntervalRecord]) -> tuple[IntervalRecord | None, bool]:
    """Return (winner, is_conflict) for candidate records of one interval."""
    if not records:
        return None, False
    best_precedence = max(precedence(r) for r in records)
    top = [r for r in records if precedence(r) == best_precedence]
    if len({r.value for r in top}) > 1:
        return None, True
    return max(top, key=_order), False
"""Batch ingestion: stage, validate and publish NEM12 data atomically.

A batch either publishes fully (records stored, current selection updated)
or is rejected with a stable error code — never a partially visible dataset.

Publication of the current selection is optimistic: candidates are first
evaluated without locks, then every affected interval is re-evaluated and
written under a per-interval row lock in deterministic order. A writer that
raced a concurrent commit therefore re-reads the winner's records instead of
publishing stale results, and equal-precedence conflicts still quarantine.
"""

import hashlib
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date, datetime

from django.db import transaction
from django.db.utils import IntegrityError
from django.utils import timezone

from taryx.core.accounts.models import Account, MeterChannel
from taryx.core.metering.models import (
    CurrentInterval,
    IngestionBatch,
    IntervalRecord,
    QuarantinedInterval,
)
from taryx.core.metering.nem12 import ChannelData, ChannelMeta, Nem12Error, parse_nem12
from taryx.core.metering.nem_time import nem_interval_end_utc
from taryx.core.metering.selection import precedence, select_current


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class IngestResult:
    batch: IngestionBatch


def _duplicate_of_original(content_hash: str, source_name: str) -> IngestionBatch:
    original = (
        IngestionBatch.objects.exclude(status=IngestionBatch.Status.DUPLICATE)
        .filter(content_sha256=content_hash)
        .get()
    )
    return IngestionBatch.objects.create(
        source_name=source_name,
        content_sha256=content_hash,
        status=IngestionBatch.Status.DUPLICATE,
        duplicate_of=original,
    )


def ingest_nem12_content(content: bytes, source_name: str) -> IngestResult:
    content_hash = hashlib.sha256(content).hexdigest()
    if (
        IngestionBatch.objects.exclude(status=IngestionBatch.Status.DUPLICATE)
        .filter(content_sha256=content_hash)
        .exists()
    ):
        return IngestResult(_duplicate_of_original(content_hash, source_name))

    try:
        text = content.decode("utf-8")
    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
        return IngestResult(
            _record_outcome(
                content_hash,
                source_name,
                IngestionBatch.Status.REJECTED,
                error_code="invalid_encoding",
                error_detail=f"bytes are not valid UTF-8: {exc}",
            )
        )

    try:
        meta, channels = parse_nem12(text)
        batch = _publish(content_hash, source_name, meta, channels)
    except Nem12Error as exc:
        batch = _record_outcome(
            content_hash,
            source_name,
            IngestionBatch.Status.REJECTED,
            error_code=exc.code,
            error_detail=str(exc),
        )
    return IngestResult(batch)


def _record_outcome(
    content_hash: str, source_name: str, status: str, **fields: object
) -> IngestionBatch:
    """Insert a batch outcome row; lose the hash race gracefully as a duplicate.

    The savepoint confines the unique-violation so the caller's transaction
    state is untouched, and the loser resolves the actual winner — published
    or rejected — rather than assuming one status.
    """
    try:
        with transaction.atomic():
            return IngestionBatch.objects.create(
                source_name=source_name,
                content_sha256=content_hash,
                status=status,
                **fields,
            )
    except IntegrityError:
        return _duplicate_of_original(content_hash, source_name)


def _publish(
    content_hash: str,
    source_name: str,
    meta: dict[tuple[str, str], ChannelMeta],
    channels: list[ChannelData],
) -> IngestionBatch:
    channel_rows = _resolve_channels(meta)
    with transaction.atomic():
        batch = _record_outcome(content_hash, source_name, IngestionBatch.Status.PUBLISHED)
        if batch.status == IngestionBatch.Status.DUPLICATE:
            return batch

        records: list[IntervalRecord] = []
        for data in channels:
            channel = channel_rows[(data.nmi, data.suffix)]
            for day in data.days:
                for item in day.values:
                    records.append(
                        IntervalRecord(
                            batch=batch,
                            channel=channel,
                            interval_date=day.interval_date,
                            interval_number=item.interval_number,
                            interval_end_utc=nem_interval_end_utc(
                                day.interval_date,
                                item.interval_number,
                                channel.interval_minutes,
                            ),
                            value=item.value,
                            quality=item.quality or "",
                            method_code=item.method_code,
                            reason_code=item.reason_code,
                            update_dt=item.update_dt,
                            msats_load_dt=item.msats_load_dt,
                            row_number=day.row_number,
                        )
                    )
        IntervalRecord.objects.bulk_create(records)

        affected = sorted({(r.channel_id, r.interval_end_utc) for r in records})
        accepted = _apply_selection(batch, affected)
        batch.record_count = len(records)
        batch.accepted_count = accepted
        batch.quarantined_count = (
            QuarantinedInterval.objects.filter(candidate_records__batch=batch).distinct().count()
        )
        batch.save(update_fields=["record_count", "accepted_count", "quarantined_count"])
    return batch


def _resolve_channels(
    meta: dict[tuple[str, str], ChannelMeta],
) -> dict[tuple[str, str], MeterChannel]:
    missing = []
    resolved: dict[tuple[str, str], MeterChannel] = {}
    for (nmi, suffix), m in meta.items():
        channel = MeterChannel.objects.filter(supply_point__nmi=nmi, suffix=suffix).first()
        if channel is None:
            missing.append(f"{nmi}:{suffix}")
        elif channel.interval_minutes != m.interval_minutes or channel.uom.lower() != m.uom.lower():
            raise Nem12Error(
                "channel_mismatch",
                f"{nmi}:{suffix} declares {m.uom}/{m.interval_minutes}min but channel "
                f"is {channel.uom}/{channel.interval_minutes}min",
            )
        else:
            resolved[(nmi, suffix)] = channel
    if missing:
        raise Nem12Error("unknown_nmi", f"unknown NMI/suffix: {', '.join(missing)}")
    return resolved


def _apply_selection(batch: IngestionBatch, affected: list[tuple[int, datetime]]) -> int:
    """Publish winners for affected intervals.

    Phase 1 evaluates candidates without locks — the read a racing publisher
    would have made. Phase 2 re-evaluates each interval under its
    CurrentInterval row lock (created on first publication via insert retry),
    so commits that landed mid-flight are seen before anything is written.
    """
    for channel_id, interval_end in affected:
        select_current(
            list(
                IntervalRecord.objects.filter(channel_id=channel_id, interval_end_utc=interval_end)
            )
        )

    accounts = {
        channel_id: account_id
        for channel_id, account_id in MeterChannel.objects.filter(
            pk__in={channel_id for channel_id, _ in affected}
        ).values_list("pk", "supply_point__account_id")
    }
    accepted = 0
    for channel_id, interval_end in affected:
        for attempt in range(3):
            try:
                with transaction.atomic():
                    accepted += _publish_interval(
                        batch, channel_id, interval_end, accounts[channel_id]
                    )
                break
            except IntegrityError:
                if attempt == 2:
                    raise
    return accepted


def _publish_interval(
    batch: IngestionBatch, channel_id: int, interval_end: datetime, account_id: int
) -> int:
    # Shared input-revision protocol: take the account row lock before any
    # mutation so billing's locked input validation serializes with this
    # publication — including quarantine inserts, which lock nothing else.
    Account.objects.select_for_update().filter(pk=account_id).exists()
    current = (
        CurrentInterval.objects.select_for_update()
        .filter(channel_id=channel_id, interval_end_utc=interval_end)
        .first()
    )
    candidates = list(
        IntervalRecord.objects.filter(channel_id=channel_id, interval_end_utc=interval_end)
    )
    winner, conflict = select_current(candidates)
    if conflict or winner is None:
        quarantine, _ = QuarantinedInterval.objects.get_or_create(
            channel_id=channel_id,
            interval_end_utc=interval_end,
            status=QuarantinedInterval.Status.OPEN,
            defaults={"detail": "equal-precedence conflicting values"},
        )
        best = max(precedence(c) for c in candidates)
        quarantine.candidate_records.add(*[c for c in candidates if precedence(c) == best])
        return 0

    if current is None:
        CurrentInterval.objects.create(
            channel_id=channel_id,
            interval_end_utc=interval_end,
            value=winner.value,
            quality=winner.quality,
            source_record=winner,
        )
    elif current.source_record_id != winner.id or current.value != winner.value:
        current.value = winner.value
        current.quality = winner.quality
        current.source_record = winner
        current.selection_version += 1
        current.save(
            update_fields=["value", "quality", "source_record", "selection_version", "updated_at"]
        )

    QuarantinedInterval.objects.filter(
        channel_id=channel_id,
        interval_end_utc=interval_end,
        status=QuarantinedInterval.Status.OPEN,
    ).update(status=QuarantinedInterval.Status.RESOLVED, resolved_at=timezone.now())
    return 1


class ResolutionError(ValueError):
    def __init__(self, code: str, detail: str):
        self.code = code
        super().__init__(detail)


def resolve_quarantine(
    quarantine_id: int, record_id: int, *, actor: str, reason: str
) -> QuarantinedInterval:
    """Approver-selected resolution for an open quarantine.

    The chosen candidate must be one of the recorded conflicting records.
    Its value is published as the current interval and the quarantine is
    closed with the actor and reason retained."""
    with transaction.atomic():
        quarantine = QuarantinedInterval.objects.filter(
            pk=quarantine_id, status=QuarantinedInterval.Status.OPEN
        ).first()
        if quarantine is None:
            raise ResolutionError("not_found", "quarantine not found or already resolved")
        # Shared input-revision protocol (see _publish_interval): the
        # account lock must precede the quarantine/interval mutations.
        account_id = (
            MeterChannel.objects.filter(pk=quarantine.channel_id)
            .values_list("supply_point__account_id", flat=True)
            .get()
        )
        Account.objects.select_for_update().filter(pk=account_id).exists()
        quarantine = QuarantinedInterval.objects.select_for_update().get(pk=quarantine_id)
        if quarantine.status != QuarantinedInterval.Status.OPEN:
            raise ResolutionError("not_found", "quarantine not found or already resolved")
        record = quarantine.candidate_records.filter(pk=record_id).first()
        if record is None:
            raise ResolutionError(
                "not_a_candidate", f"record {record_id} is not a quarantine candidate"
            )
        current = (
            CurrentInterval.objects.select_for_update()
            .filter(
                channel_id=quarantine.channel_id,
                interval_end_utc=quarantine.interval_end_utc,
            )
            .first()
        )
        if current is None:
            CurrentInterval.objects.create(
                channel_id=quarantine.channel_id,
                interval_end_utc=quarantine.interval_end_utc,
                value=record.value,
                quality=record.quality,
                source_record=record,
            )
        else:
            current.value = record.value
            current.quality = record.quality
            current.source_record = record
            current.selection_version += 1
            current.save(
                update_fields=[
                    "value",
                    "quality",
                    "source_record",
                    "selection_version",
                    "updated_at",
                ]
            )
        quarantine.status = QuarantinedInterval.Status.RESOLVED
        quarantine.resolved_at = timezone.now()
        quarantine.detail = f"{quarantine.detail} | resolved by {actor}: {reason}".strip(" |")
        quarantine.save(update_fields=["status", "resolved_at", "detail"])
    return quarantine


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ChannelCoverage:
    channel_id: int
    expected: int
    selected: int
    quarantined: int

    @property
    def complete(self) -> bool:
        return self.selected == self.expected and self.quarantined == 0


def channel_coverage(channel: MeterChannel, start_date: date, end_date: date) -> ChannelCoverage:
    """Interval coverage for [start_date, end_date) NEM days.

    Billing calls this to reject incomplete coverage rather than silently
    rating partial data.
    """
    days = (end_date - start_date).days
    if days <= 0:
        raise ValueError("end_date must be after start_date")
    per_day = (24 * 60) // channel.interval_minutes
    start_utc = nem_interval_end_utc(start_date, 0, channel.interval_minutes)
    end_utc = nem_interval_end_utc(end_date, 0, channel.interval_minutes)
    selected = CurrentInterval.objects.filter(
        channel=channel, interval_end_utc__gt=start_utc, interval_end_utc__lte=end_utc
    ).count()
    quarantined = QuarantinedInterval.objects.filter(
        channel=channel,
        interval_end_utc__gt=start_utc,
        interval_end_utc__lte=end_utc,
        status=QuarantinedInterval.Status.OPEN,
    ).count()
    return ChannelCoverage(channel.id, days * per_day, selected, quarantined)
"""Rating orchestration: gather immutable inputs, pin them, rate, persist.

Coverage, agreement resolution and error policy live here; the arithmetic
in engine.py stays pure and independently testable. Tariff specs are
injected by the caller (territory/client policy packages, wired in
composition) so core never imports outer layers.
"""

import hashlib
import json
from datetime import date, timedelta
from decimal import Decimal

from django.db import transaction

from taryx.core.accounts.models import Account, MeterChannel
from taryx.core.metering.ingestion import channel_coverage
from taryx.core.metering.models import CurrentInterval, QuarantinedInterval
from taryx.core.metering.nem_time import nem_interval_end_utc, nem_local
from taryx.core.pricing.engine import (
    ENGINE_VERSION,
    AgreementSpan,
    ChannelSlice,
    IntervalQty,
    RatingError,
    rate,
)
from taryx.core.pricing.models import RatingLine, RatingRun
from taryx.core.pricing.tariffs import TariffSpec


def _input_payload(
    *,
    account: Account,
    period_start: date,
    period_end: date,
    agreements: list[AgreementSpan],
    tariffs: dict[str, TariffSpec],
    channels: list[tuple[MeterChannel, list]],
    quarantines: list[QuarantinedInterval],
    gst_rate: Decimal,
    policy_identity: str,
) -> dict:
    """The exact inputs a rating consumes — hashed into input_digest and
    retained verbatim on the run so historical calculations stay
    reconstructible even if referenced metadata rows later change."""
    return {
        "account": account.reference,
        "period": [period_start.isoformat(), period_end.isoformat()],
        "engine_version": ENGINE_VERSION,
        "policy_identity": policy_identity,
        "gst_rate": str(gst_rate),
        "agreements": [
            {
                "id": a.agreement_id,
                "tariff_code": a.tariff_code,
                "version": a.version,
                "effective_from": a.effective_from.isoformat(),
                "effective_to": a.effective_to.isoformat() if a.effective_to else None,
            }
            for a in sorted(agreements, key=lambda a: a.agreement_id)
        ],
        "tariffs": {
            code: {
                "version": spec.version,
                "supply_per_day": str(spec.supply_per_day),
                "import_bands": [
                    [
                        b.name,
                        str(b.price),
                        ([b.window[0].isoformat(), b.window[1].isoformat()] if b.window else None),
                    ]
                    for b in spec.import_bands
                ],
                "export_credit_per_kwh": (
                    str(spec.export_credit_per_kwh) if spec.export_credit_per_kwh else None
                ),
                "gst_exempt": spec.gst_exempt,
            }
            for code, spec in sorted(tariffs.items())
        },
        "channels": [
            {
                "channel_id": channel.id,
                "suffix": channel.suffix,
                "direction": channel.direction,
                "records": [
                    [
                        row.interval_end_utc.isoformat(),
                        str(row.value),
                        row.quality,
                        row.source_record_id,
                        row.source_record.interval_date.isoformat(),
                    ]
                    for row in rows
                ],
            }
            for channel, rows in sorted(channels, key=lambda c: c[0].id)
        ],
        "quarantines": [
            [q.id, q.channel_id, q.interval_end_utc.isoformat()]
            for q in sorted(quarantines, key=lambda q: q.id)
        ],
    }


def _input_digest(payload: dict) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()


def _gather_inputs(
    account: Account, period_start: date, period_end: date, *, lock: bool = False
) -> tuple[
    list[AgreementSpan],
    list[tuple[MeterChannel, list[CurrentInterval]]],
    list[QuarantinedInterval],
]:
    """Selected interval rows, open quarantines and agreement spans pinning
    a rating period.

    With lock=True every row feeding the digest is locked FOR UPDATE —
    billing holds those locks from final validation through commit so no
    input-changing writer can interleave. Mutating paths (interval
    publication, quarantine resolution) take the account row lock first,
    which is what prevents a concurrent *insert* of a new quarantine from
    slipping between validation and commit.
    """
    channel_rows: list[tuple[MeterChannel, list[CurrentInterval]]] = []
    quarantines: list[QuarantinedInterval] = []
    for channel in MeterChannel.objects.filter(supply_point__account=account).order_by("id"):
        start_utc = nem_interval_end_utc(period_start, 0, channel.interval_minutes)
        end_utc = nem_interval_end_utc(period_end, 0, channel.interval_minutes)
        interval_qs = CurrentInterval.objects.filter(
            channel=channel,
            interval_end_utc__gt=start_utc,
            interval_end_utc__lte=end_utc,
        ).select_related("source_record")
        if lock:
            interval_qs = interval_qs.select_for_update(of=("self",))
        rows = list(interval_qs.order_by("interval_end_utc"))
        channel_rows.append((channel, rows))
        quarantine_qs = QuarantinedInterval.objects.filter(
            channel=channel,
            interval_end_utc__gt=start_utc,
            interval_end_utc__lte=end_utc,
            status=QuarantinedInterval.Status.OPEN,
        )
        if lock:
            quarantine_qs = quarantine_qs.select_for_update()
        quarantines.extend(quarantine_qs.order_by("id"))
    agreement_qs = account.tariff_agreements.all()
    if lock:
        agreement_qs = agreement_qs.select_for_update()
    agreements = [
        AgreementSpan(
            agreement_id=a.id,
            tariff_code=a.tariff_code,
            version=a.version,
            effective_from=a.effective_from,
            effective_to=a.effective_to,
        )
        for a in agreement_qs
    ]
    return agreements, channel_rows, quarantines


def lock_inputs(account: Account, period_start: date, period_end: date) -> None:
    """Shared revision protocol for input-changing writers.

    Acquires, in order, the account row lock then every row feeding this
    period's input digest. Callers must hold these locks from the final
    digest validation through transaction commit; publishers and
    quarantine resolution acquire the same account lock first so any
    input change either lands before (and is re-validated) or waits
    until the financial transaction commits.
    """
    Account.objects.select_for_update().filter(pk=account.pk).exists()
    _gather_inputs(account, period_start, period_end, lock=True)


def compute_input_digest(
    account: Account,
    period_start: date,
    period_end: date,
    *,
    tariffs: dict[str, TariffSpec],
    gst_rate: Decimal,
    policy_identity: str,
) -> str:
    """Digest of the inputs a rating over this period would consume now."""
    agreements, channel_rows, quarantines = _gather_inputs(account, period_start, period_end)
    return _input_digest(
        _input_payload(
            account=account,
            period_start=period_start,
            period_end=period_end,
            agreements=agreements,
            tariffs=tariffs,
            channels=channel_rows,
            quarantines=quarantines,
            gst_rate=gst_rate,
            policy_identity=policy_identity,
        )
    )


def rate_account(
    account: Account,
    period_start: date,
    period_end: date,
    *,
    tariffs: dict[str, TariffSpec],
    gst_rate: Decimal,
    policy_identity: str,
) -> RatingRun:
    """Rate [period_start, period_end) NEM days and persist the pinned run."""
    days = [period_start + timedelta(days=i) for i in range((period_end - period_start).days)]
    if not days:
        raise RatingError("empty_period", "period must cover at least one day")

    agreements, channel_rows, quarantines = _gather_inputs(account, period_start, period_end)

    slices: list[ChannelSlice] = []
    for channel, rows in channel_rows:
        coverage = channel_coverage(channel, period_start, period_end)
        if not coverage.complete:
            raise RatingError(
                "incomplete_coverage",
                f"{channel}: {coverage.selected}/{coverage.expected} intervals, "
                f"{coverage.quarantined} quarantined",
            )
        slices.append(
            ChannelSlice(
                channel_id=channel.id,
                suffix=channel.suffix,
                direction=channel.direction,
                intervals=tuple(
                    IntervalQty(
                        day=row.source_record.interval_date,
                        end_tod=nem_local(row.interval_end_utc).time(),
                        value=row.value,
                    )
                    for row in rows
                ),
            )
        )

    calc = rate(
        days=days,
        agreements=agreements,
        tariffs=tariffs,
        channels=slices,
        gst_rate=gst_rate,
    )

    payload = _input_payload(
        account=account,
        period_start=period_start,
        period_end=period_end,
        agreements=agreements,
        tariffs=tariffs,
        channels=channel_rows,
        quarantines=quarantines,
        gst_rate=gst_rate,
        policy_identity=policy_identity,
    )

    with transaction.atomic():
        run = RatingRun.objects.create(
            account=account,
            period_start=period_start,
            period_end=period_end,
            engine_version=ENGINE_VERSION,
            policy_identity=policy_identity,
            input_digest=_input_digest(payload),
            input_snapshot=payload,
            net=calc.net,
            gst=calc.gst,
            total=calc.total,
        )
        RatingLine.objects.bulk_create(
            RatingLine(
                run=run,
                sequence=index,
                agreement_id=line.agreement_id,
                tariff_code=line.tariff_code,
                segment_from=line.segment_from,
                segment_to=line.segment_to,
                element=line.element,
                band=line.band,
                quantity=line.quantity,
                unit=line.unit,
                rate=line.rate,
                amount=line.amount,
                gst=line.gst,
                basis=line.basis,
            )
            for index, line in enumerate(calc.lines, start=1)
        )
    return run
